quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

20 Questions • Passing Score 14

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?

options.text: Road signs.
Pedestrians.
Other motorists.
Street lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians are harder to see at night than signs and other roadside objects.

questions.question: A pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane is crossing the street. What should you do?

options.text: You must always yield the right-of-way.
You must tell them where to cross the street.
You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog shows that a pedestrian is blind or partially blind. You must always yield the right-of-way to them.

questions.question: Before driving, a driver taking an over-the-counter drug should:

options.text: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
Drink alcohol instead.
Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.
Drive only during daylight hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the labels on the drug before driving.
questions.explanation: Over-the-counter medications can affect your ability to drive safely. Always check the label for warnings about driving. Ask your doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure.

questions.question: A tire suddenly blows out while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
Pump the brakes rapidly.
Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and take your foot off the accelerator. Apply the brakes lightly when safe. Do not move to the shoulder until the car has slowed down.

questions.question: What do construction zone signs look like?

options.text: Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.
questions.explanation: Temporary work zone signs have an orange background with black letters or symbols. They are placed on the right side of the road, or on both sides on divided highways.

questions.question: What can happen when alcohol is mixed with another drug?

options.text: The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.
Nothing will happen.
The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be reduced.
The effects of only the alcohol may be reduced.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of the alcohol and the drug may both be increased.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and another drug together can make both effects stronger. For example, one drink while taking a cold remedy can affect you like several drinks.

questions.question: What can happen if you take a prescription drug and drink alcohol?

options.text: There will likely be no effect.
It will make you more alert.
It can make you unfit to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make you unfit to drive.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair your driving ability. They are especially dangerous when combined with alcohol.

questions.question: Where may you not park?

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the road's edge.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: There is a 35 mph speed zone after the curve ahead.
Drive no slower than 35 mph around the upcoming curve.
Slow down to 35 mph or less for the upcoming curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to 35 mph or less for the upcoming curve.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about immediate road conditions ahead. Speed advisory plaques show the recommended speed for the upcoming condition.

questions.question: Which action commonly causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Exceeding the speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.
Getting adequate rest and staying alert.
Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Exceeding the speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit or too fast for conditions commonly causes crashes. Always drive with traffic flow and within legal speed limits.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Traffic light ahead.
Do not pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass other vehicles. If there is a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line, drivers on the solid yellow side cannot pass. If both lines are solid, no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Side road.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What helps someone get over the effects of drinking alcohol?

options.text: Tomato juice and lime
Hot coffee
Fresh air
Only time

questions.correctAnswerText: Only time
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person overcome the effects of alcohol. Nothing else can speed up this process.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four-lane traffic ahead.
Divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.
Intersection ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two-way traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is moving in both directions ahead.

questions.question: What safety restraints work best in a crash?

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Only an airbag.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
No safety restraints.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts double your chance of surviving a crash and greatly reduce serious injury. Airbags work best when used together with safety belts. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: What should you do if your car breaks down on a highway?

options.text: Stay in your car and wait for help.
Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
Honk your horn at passing cars.
Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your four-way flashers to warn other drivers.
questions.explanation: Turn on your hazard flashers right away. Move your car as far off the road as possible. Pop your hood so other drivers know your car is disabled.

questions.question: What happens when you tailgate (drive too close behind another car)?

options.text: It can anger other drivers.
You cannot get a traffic ticket for it.
It prevents other cars from cutting you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can anger other drivers.
questions.explanation: Tailgating is unsafe and can anger other drivers. It may lead to aggressive driving. You can get a traffic ticket for driving unsafely.

questions.question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is crossing the street. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until they are far away from your path.
Honk and drive past them.
Carefully drive around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are far away from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind person using a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop until they are completely away from your vehicle. Always give them the right-of-way.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Honk and keep your speed.
Speed up to get past them quickly.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who may cross your path. When you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: Do not pass another vehicle.
You may pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
You may pass if you know the road ahead.
You may pass, but only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. You must follow its instructions. This sign means passing is not allowed in this area.
